newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes up on oversold signals, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes up on oversold signals, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply higher on fund buying tied to signals the market was oversold plus some concern about reports of drier weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"Weather has become a factor in central Illinois and around St. Louis," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "There's hot weather as we go into pollination for corn. We're on a hot, dry trend into the weekend."
The weather was not an overriding concern right now but there was substantial discussion about the warmer pattern.

"Starting next week, on into August we'll be pollinating and the weather is looking a little more uncertain," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities, Des Moines, Iowa. "We don't have much risk premium in corn."

Technicians cited the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the July which fell Monday to a recent low of just below 19 percent and closed Tuesday at 44 percent. An RSI of 30 percent or less indicates an oversold market.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 6-1/2 at $2.49-3/4 a bushel. New crop December closed 7-1/2 cents higher at $2.37-1/4.
Short covering before Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report and Friday's supply/demand report was cited.
Funds bought at least 25.0 million bushels of corn, traders said. Refco Inc bought 11.0 million bushels of December, traders said.
Commercial selling limited gains with Cargill Inc selling four million bushels of December and Produce Grain sold three million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, Term Commodities did one million bushels of December/July at 13 to 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 87,000 contracts, above the 80,787 traded Tuesday.
In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,500 December $2.30 puts at 7-3/4 to 8-1/4 cents, traders said. Griffin Trading bought 700 December $2.50 puts at 22 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 26,000 contracts, below the 27,005 traded Tuesday.
